clue.text: Beat up game

indicators.note: in a down clue 'up' means the word for beat is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to beat someone is to flog them

explanation.surface: A game that got knocked about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns FLOG upside down in this down entry, giving the game.
explanation.definitionFit: Golf is a sport played with clubs and a ball over a course.

clue.text: Might sound a very small offering

indicators.note: 'sound' tells us to say the clue word out loud and write what we hear

parts.note: the clue word itself, spoken

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone could make only a tiny donation.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'widow's mite' of the Bible story was a tiny coin she gave, so a mite is a small offering.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospel story a poor widow gives two mites, coins of minimal value, to the temple treasury.

clue.text: Dig into a drawer for cash

definitions.meaning: to ... ground is to dig or plough it

explanation.surface: Someone rummages in a cash drawer for money.
explanation.definitionFit: Farmers prepare soil by tilling, and a shop keeps its takings in the register drawer of that name.

clue.text: Produce an order to evict tenants

definitions.meaning: a command to throw occupants out of a property

explanation.surface: A landlord issues an eviction notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A factory makes goods, and a landlord throws tenants onto the street; the same phrasal verb covers both.

clue.text: Specified plan supported by a former Tory leader

indicators.note: in a down clue, being supported means the following pieces sit underneath

parts.note: a plan is a design
Ted Heath led the Conservative Party and was Prime Minister in the 1970s

explanation.surface: A scheme backed by an ex-leader of the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: TED is Edward Heath, British Conservative leader 1965-75.
explanation.definitionFit: Something designated has been named or set apart for a particular purpose.

clue.text: Concern for loneliness found around the Channel Islands

indicators.note: the word for loneliness is found wrapped around the abbreviation for the islands

parts.note: loneliness is solitude
CI is the standard abbreviation for the Channel Islands

explanation.surface: Worry about isolation among islanders in the English Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Channel Islands, Jersey and Guernsey among them, sit between England and France.
explanation.definitionFit: Solicitude is anxious care or attentiveness for someone's welfare.

clue.text: Such an approach is needed for entire GCE revision

indicators.note: revision means reworking, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
GCE is the General Certificate of Education, the old British school exams

explanation.surface: Studying for the whole of one's GCE exams needs a vigorous approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision' hides as exam preparation but signals the anagram. GCE was the British school exam system (O and A levels) before GCSEs.
explanation.definitionFit: A vigorous, lively approach full of drive is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Robe designed for an Afrikaner

indicators.note: designed as in fashioned anew, so the letters are re-made in a new order

explanation.surface: A garment made for a South African.
explanation.definitionFit: Boers were Dutch-descended settlers of South Africa, ancestors of today's Afrikaners.

clue.text: Spanish foot-slogger

parts.note: read not as a marching soldier but as a punishment of Spanish origin that slogs, or beats, the soles of the feet

explanation.surface: An infantryman from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A foot-slogger is normally an infantryman; here 'slog' means hit, and the punishment beats the feet with a stick (Spanish baston).
explanation.definitionFit: This form of torture caned the soles of the feet; its name comes from Spanish words for a stick.

clue.text: Priceless old weapon employed by no one else

parts.note: something that costs nothing is free
the lance was a knight's long spear

explanation.surface: A valuable antique arm not used by anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Priceless' suggests invaluable, but here it means costing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-employed worker sells services to many clients and has no permanent boss.

clue.text: Half of a lovely cathedral city

indicators.note: half of the word lovely is taken, here its back three letters

explanation.surface: A charming spot in a cathedral town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ely is a small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Its great Norman cathedral, the 'Ship of the Fens', makes this English town a city.

clue.text: Field Marshal able to slip out of tight corners

definitions.meaning: William ..., British commander in Burma in the Second World War

definitions.text: able to slip out of tight corners
definitions.meaning: thin enough to squeeze through narrow gaps

explanation.surface: A slippery senior commander who always escapes trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: Field Marshal Viscount Slim led the British 14th Army in Burma.
explanation.definitionFit: A British Field Marshal bore the name, and a slender person can wriggle through narrow spaces.

clue.text: Retired sailor who deserted ship

indicators.note: retired here means going backwards, so the word for sailor is turned round

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: An ex-seaman who abandoned his vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Rats are said to desert a sinking ship, so the defining phrase is a nod to the proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbially, rodents flee a sinking vessel, and a deserter is called by that animal's name.

clue.text: Green and Milne wrote when we were this

definitions.text: Milne wrote when we were this
definitions.meaning: A. A. Milne's children's poetry book 'When We Were ...'

explanation.surface: Two authors writing about childhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like another writer next to Milne, but it means youthful. Milne's 1924 verse collection completes the title.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexperienced youth is called green, and Milne's poems were for childhood.

clue.text: Performers who take their bows before the performance commences

definitions.text: Performers who take their bows before the performance commences

parts.words: Performers who take their bows before the performance commences
parts.note: bows are not curtsies at the end but the sticks string players pick up before they begin

explanation.surface: Actors who take a curtain call before the show starts.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking a bow normally follows a show; here the bows are the instruments' bows.
explanation.definitionFit: Orchestral string players pick up their bows before playing begins.

clue.text: Thought echoed like…

definitions.meaning: sent back, as sound or light is

explanation.surface: An idea that resonates, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs the clue on to 15-down: the yodel is a cry thrown back by the hills.
explanation.definitionFit: To mull something over is to ponder it, and a mirror or a cliff sends back light or sound.

clue.text: … a far cry from the hills

definitions.text: a far cry from the hills

parts.words: a far cry from the hills
parts.note: not the idiom for a big difference but a literal call carried far from mountainsides

explanation.surface: Something very different from the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A far cry from' is an idiom for very different; here it is a loud call in the Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpine herders call across valleys in a warbling voice that carries great distances.

clue.text: Young William leaves billions to radicals currently charged

indicators.note: leaves means departs from, so these letters are removed from billions

parts.note: Bill is the familiar short form of William

explanation.surface: Little Bill bequeaths a fortune to political extremists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radicals' look political but are chemistry, and 'currently' hints at electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: These are atoms or groups bearing an electric charge, which chemists once called radicals.

clue.text: Pass on information obtained from National Front unit in cypher

indicators.note: in means the other letters are put inside the word for cypher

parts.note: a cypher is a code
NF is the abbreviation for the National Front, a British far-right party
I, the Roman numeral, is one or a unit

explanation.surface: Intelligence gathered from a coded far-right cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Front is a British far-right party.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell a secret privately to someone is to entrust them with it.

clue.text: Difficulties through which coastal vessels pass

definitions.meaning: narrow sea channels between land masses

explanation.surface: Ships hugging the shore meet trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a tight spot is being in dire trouble, and narrow channels like Dover's carry shipping.

clue.text: Cut off a personal confession of tardiness

definitions.meaning: split as three words, '...', someone admitting being behind time

explanation.surface: Someone stranded admits running behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: say the letters as 'I, so late'.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep a patient apart is to quarantine them, and split up the letters read as a late-comer's apology.

clue.text: Fair option for the guilty party

definitions.meaning: a money penalty a court may impose

explanation.surface: A just choice for someone convicted.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather that is bright is called fair, and a convicted offender may pay a penalty in money.

clue.text: Sullivan's mislaid notes?

parts.note: Arthur Sullivan's famous song about a missing musical harmony, read as notes that went astray

explanation.surface: The composer has lost his sheet music.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Sullivan, of Gilbert and Sullivan, wrote the Victorian parlour song 'The Lost Chord'.
explanation.definitionFit: Sullivan's song tells of a heavenly harmony heard once and never found again.

clue.text: It is used for digging us out of the house

indicators.note: out of means these two letters are taken away from the word for a dwelling

explanation.surface: A garden tool, which gets us out of the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove US from HOUSE to leave the tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A gardener uses this long-handled tool to break up soil and weed.

clue.text: Pass a senior officer

explanation.surface: A high-ranking officer gets through.
explanation.definitionFit: A dip between mountain peaks is called by this French-derived word, also short for colonel.

clue.text: Food fad conference

explanation.surface: A meeting about the latest eating trend.
explanation.definitionFit: A slimming regime is a diet, and some parliaments and historic assemblies bear the same name.

clue.text: How they feel if I upset everybody and pull their legs

indicators.note: upset as in overturned, so the word for everybody is turned backwards

parts.note: everybody means all
to pull someone's leg is to tease them

explanation.surface: People feel uneasy when I upset them and joke at their expense.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncomfortable, awkward people are said to feel this way when unsettled.

clue.text: Kind way to communicate if one's handwriting is illegible

definitions.text: way to communicate if one's handwriting is illegible
definitions.meaning: printing letters on a keyboard instead of writing

explanation.surface: Typing is a kind fix for bad handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sort or category is one sense; keyboarding text is the other, a fix for scrawl.

clue.text: Gets on for ever such a long time

definitions.text: for ever such a long time

explanation.surface: Someone takes forever to grow old.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone growing older is getting on, and a long while is 'for donkey's years'.

clue.text: Looked like seed potatoes

definitions.meaning: seed potatoes have buds called eyes

explanation.surface: Someone studied the seed potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: To watch something is to look at it, and potato buds are called eyes.

clue.text: Boss dedicated to raising the stock

definitions.meaning: a raised knob or ... on a surface

explanation.surface: A manager devoted to raising the share price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' looks like a manager but means a knob, and 'stock' is livestock, not shares.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative knob is a boss, and a horse-breeding establishment is a stud farm.

clue.text: Crack up and attend theatrical performances

explanation.surface: Someone breaks down and goes to the theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Losing emotional control is falling apart, and plays are theatrical works one can attend.
